#1516. Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

It was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

England were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

Gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a big mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,

[And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We showed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.

Eze just overcooks the pass that would have released Gibbs-White to run through on goal.

That was Bellingham’s third assist and should it stay 7-0 after two minutes of stoppage time, it will be Croatia’s heaviest defeat.

Nice line from the englandstats.com X account - who said you can’t win anything with kids… watching. Although quite a lot of them have now headed for the exits. This has been remarkable.

Croatia 0 England 7 (Rogers) He barely celebrates but it was a finish off the highest class. He bent his run to make Jakic play him onside, ran down the left when through one-on-one, feigned to cut in then rounded the keeper on the outside to shoot crisply into the open net as Livakovic, who has not been at fault all night, scrambled desperately.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Lewis-Skelly → HallGibbs-White → Anderson.

Bellingham and Eze are playing through the middle now with Rogers down the left.

England really ought to be in double figures by now.

Saka spurns a chance for his hat-trick at the back post when teed up with a Rogers cross from the left.

“He’s like a grown man playing against children, giving them a pat on the head as he goes past them.”

England have been magnificent going forward and with their press. Croatia have been shambolic. Bilic lasted six years in his first stint in the job. He’ll be lucky to last six months in this spell if this is the level of his players’ commitment.

Racking my brains to recall the last time England played this well against a leading nation, against any nation in fact. Maybe it was the 3-2 win away over Spain, again in the Nations League in 2018?

Croatia 0 England 4 (Saka) It’s as if Croatia have thrown in the towel. They let Gordon run in behind again on the left and pass to Bellingham who faces up Modric, jinks to his left, shimmies with a wiggle of the shoulder to beat him down the side and then centre to Saka who taps it in, left alone by the negligent Vuskovic and Gvardiol.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

Blimey! Kovacic has just missed an open goal as he exploited a lack of concentration at the back by Anderson to blindside him and take the ball off him to dribble to his right through the box with Pickford scrambling like crazy. Once he had opened up the gap to shoot through from the right of the penalty spot, he speared it inches wide. The crowd could not be more deflated if you poked them with a hat-pin.

A STUNNING miss from Mateo Kovačić 🫣The Man City man rounds the keeper and misses an open goal. pic.twitter.com/YfPuDehwYf

I wonder if Luka Modric has ever been in the position where he has not been the best player on the pitch in a headband? Well tonight he’s not, as Alex Scott has been excellent on his first England start. He’s pressed high, dropped deep, won the ball back, beaten his man. It’s just amazing it’s taken Tuchel this long to start him.

I think a few of us (me included) might have thought Trent Alexander-Arnold was the only England full-back who could have provided the cross for Gordon to score against the Czech Republic. Well we were wrong, as Quansah produced a carbon copy of Trent’s cross for Gordon to score with his head against Croatia. Who knew he had that in his locker?

Croatia 0 England 3 (Gordon) His goal on Tuesday was a very rare header and now he’s added a second. Kane sent Quansah down the right and the right-back whipped over a cross that Gordon allowed to bounce in front of him and then flopped rather than dived forward to bury at the back post. He’s the new Nat Lofthouse.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

A spell of possession beyond 30 seconds for Croatia for the first time. Scott is in the right place to intercept and scupper the first thrust and then Pickford comes a long way off his line and has a bit of a flap at a cross but gets enough of his fist on it, even if he misjudged the flight, to get away with it.

Bilic has sent his outfield subs to warm up. Might be some damage limitation imminent. Modric, if he is to play, ought to be as a 10 not in this deep role.

The young locals are growing restless now. Bood greeted England’s second goal and it felt they were directed at Croatia, rather than the England team. England’s 100-strong band of supporters are making themselves heard and are witnessing an excellent performance so far.

Thomas Tuchel could not believe Anthony Gordon did not kill the game from Bellingham’s cross. He turned to the bench when the ball did not hit the back of the net and angrily remonstrated about the fact England had not scored. He wants this game done and dusted while his team are so dominant.

The tide is relentless. Konsa miscues Saka’s cross from a  free-kick behind for a goal-kick and moments later Anderson, flooding into acres of vacated space, blazes over from 20 yards.

England are playing with the fluency and swagger of a side that are 5-0 up. In fact they could well have been. Kane’s goal was his 88th for England. Bellingham’s his 14th.

Bellingham quickly returns the favour to Gordon with a brilliant run down the right. Gordon checks his run then bends it past Vuskovic’s shoulder to receive the curling cross but he clips it from six yards straight into Livakovic’s chest as the goalkeeper spread himself starfish style.

Croatia 0 England 2 (Bellingham) A Clásico goal. Saka’s cross from the right, looking for Kane again, is overhit. But Gordon is there to trap it on the volley, take it down then slip a clever pass to Bellingham who pokes it past Livakovic. England are off to a flyer. Barcelona assist → Real Madrid finish.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

England tear a hole through the heart of the Croatia defence again. Modric and Kovacic are just being swamped. Gordon, who was on the underlap as Hall brought it forward, pings the pass from the middle out to Saka who faces up Perisic and whips an inswinging cross with his left to the back post that Vuskovic juts gets to before Kane to glance it behind.

This is seriously the best I have seen England move the ball in a very long time. Their passing is slick and quick and they are so dangerous. Alex Scott is making a real difference in midfield. Feels strange it has taken Thomas Tuchel until now to start him but he is making a real impression and played a clever part in Harry Kane’s excellent team goal.

Another heart-in-mouth moment for the Croatia defence when Kane, drifting out to the right, arrows in the perfect cross that sits up nicely for Saka to toe towards goal from close range. It dribbles past the post and the flag goes up to spare his recriminations.

England have started this game brilliantly, but Croatia have been woeful. They’ve barely strung a pass together and should be two goals down already.

England almost make it two in two minutes when their high press, vigorously applied, forces another error and allows Anderson tos end Gordon racing behind Stanisic down the left. Saka keeps pace with him through the middle but Gordon, in the form of his life, is never going to lay it off and hammers a shot instead that Livakovic turns away.

And that is exactly why it pays to warm-up seriously. Kane was lethal in the pre-match warm-up, see my earlier post, and finished his first chance in the game superbly. Practice makes perfect.

Croatia 0 England 1 (Kane) Gvardiol brings the ball out of the area to the left then sprays a pass into the centre-circle that his City team-mate, Guehi, intercepts. Guehi passes it to Scott who shifts it quickly upfield to Bellingham and the No10 slips a delightful reverse pass between the left-back and centre-half into Kane’s path. The England captain calmly lifts his shot over Livakovic and high into the net.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

Sucic is penalised for a sliding tackle on Bellingham that legs up the England forward in full flight down the left. Saka takes it, crossing on a shallow arc to the 18-yard line. Guéhi cushions a header but too close to a defender for Kane to pounce.

Anderson takes the corner short and Croatia defend the belated cross.

Looks like the Croatian kids were busy in art and English classed this week, as they unfurled a banner that read ‘It’s not coming home’ in one side of the ground as the game kicked off.

England attack up the left patiently, turning back when necessary. Kane drops deep and fires a pass to Bellingham who plays it down the inside-left for Gordon who runs beyond Vuskovic and rakes a left-foot shot that Livakovic, his Cam Nou team-mate, turns behind.

Alex Scott is given the first kick of the game, knocks it all the way back to Pickford who pumps it so long that Livakovic comes for it and makes a mess of it, shanking it out for a throw-in.

The Croatia national anthem is belted out. Croatia are heart-clutchers when they sing their anthem. It seems an increasingly common practice.

And it does sound like a schoolboy international. England are in red shirts and navy shorts, Croatia in their white and red chequerboard.

You can hear the players singing the national anthem.

Three sides of the ground are now full of small children – and some bigger children who look suspiciously like adults. There’s every chance that I either end this game with a headache or running away from a pack of dogs, given the high-pitched home support.

I just watched Anthony Barry put on a finishing drill with some of the England players. The standard was pretty high, but the quality of Kane’s finishing was, unsurprisingly, superb. He scored with seven of his eight shots past James Trafford and Jason Steele. The one shot he didn’t score with forced Steele into an excellent save. You often see players go through the motions in the pre-match warm-up, but not Kane. He hit every shot like he was trying to win the game in the 90th minute. England’s starters have now gone in ahead of kick-off.

[The camp] has been very good, helped us unwind and recharge the batteries after two intense matches. We have been on the road for a few days, the setting was beautiful. Now we need to switch on which is very difficult [because] the atmosphere is very different with 6,000 children in the stadium. We want to make it a really competitive game but the surrounding is very different. I think wee are up for it.

[Alex Scott] did so well in training and did so well when he made his debut so he brings the full package. He has legs, good at defending, good in the high press, smooth on the ball and good decision-making. That is why he has our trust.

It was a close decision [over Alexander-Arnold] but we decided for Jarrell to start. We will have a lot to defend especially on that side with Perisic and Jarrell did well with Bukayo. We have Trent as an option from the bench.

We need a complete performance in all aspects, adapt to the circumstances. Our physicality, if it is a real competitive match then we would have the edge. Now it feels more like an open training session with the environment and that will suit them better.

But I hope we can bring the intensity and then have the edge.

"To be fair, I don't care" 🤷‍♂️😂Never change, Slaven Bilić 🇭🇷 pic.twitter.com/hBrtZ5TiBy

Loud (high-pitched) cheers for the Croatia team from children inside the Rijeka Stadium. Luka Modric, aged 41, is starting for the home team. He’s a year older than Wayne Rooney, who retired from international football nine years ago. The England players were booed when they entered the pitch. These kids know what they are doing.

I was here eight years ago when it really was a behind-closed-doors game for England. This is very different. There are around 6,000 Croatian children, with their guardians, here and the stands are filling up. It’s also pretty noisy with all the pre-match music.

In 2018, we could hear exactly what the managers and players were shouting – Jordan Henderson was particularly loud – but I don’t think that will be the case this time around. The noise from the fans may be quite high pitched today, but I don’t think it will be quiet at all.

England have 100 fans here and, mercifully, they have not been forced to watch from inside the metal caged away end. They haven’t been allowed to bring in England flags, so it’s currently quite hard to locate exactly where they are.

Croatia Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Perisic; Modric, Kovacic; Ivanovic, P Sucic, Baturina; Musa.Substitutes Pandur, Kotarski, Smolcic, Sutalo, Kramaric, Vlasic, Mario Pasalic, Jakic, Marco Pasalic, Matanovic, Luka Sucic, Misic.

England Pickford; Quansah, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall; Anderson, Scott; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.Substitutes Trafford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Chalobah, Ngumoha, Branthwaite, Lewis-Skelly, Rogers, Garner, Calvert-Lewin, Gibbs-White, Eze.

Thomas Tuchel was glowing about Alex Scott in his pre-match media duties ahead of today’s game against Croatia and the midfielder has been handed his first England start.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Tuchel had taken Scott to the United States on his pre-World Cup training camp, but the Bournemouth midfielder was not part of the squad for the tournament-proper.

On Scott, Tuchel said: “I am super impressed by Alex Scott, I think he is at the moment one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and he just proves it in every training session. He had a fantastic debut the other day and really really impressed me.”

🇭🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Croatia's starting XI vs. England!Petar Musa and Martin Baturina get their first starts under Slaven Bilić! pic.twitter.com/dPt32fiXbh

Your #ThreeLions for Saturday night 🔴🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/A2M4lMfBNj

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has said Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s new goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

Uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Advertisement | GambleAware | 18+ Betting on the football tonight? Take a look at these tips and offers chosen by Telegraph Media Group

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

#1515. “Like Pio Esposito” – Camarda’s impatience questioned by ex-Milan Futuro coach Oddo

Massimo Oddo has admitted that Francesco Camarda has unquestionable talent, but suggested there has been some impatience regarding his development.

Going into the 2025-26 season, the decision was made to send Camarda out on loan to Lecce, where he had a mixed campaign to say the least. He did score his first ever Serie A goal, but played second fiddle for large spells until a shoulder injury saw him miss an extended period.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim arrived and decided that he wished to keep the 18-year-old around, believing that he is ready to be the deputy to Goncalo Ramos, the new club-record signing. The Portuguese is struggling for goals, while Camarda is struggling for minutes, leading to suggestions of a new loan in January.

Oddo knows Camarda well having been the head coach of Milan Futuro during their first season in Serie C and then in Serie D following their relegation. Speaking to La Repubblica, he gave his take on the forward’s current situation.

“The talent hasn’t disappeared, but you have to be patient. I take Camarda as an example, one of the most promising centre-forwards I’ve ever seen,” he said (via Calciomercato.com).

“He couldn’t wait and paid the price for his early leap to Serie A. He should have taken a more gradual path, like Pio Esposito. In general, I’m concerned about the excessive power of agents.”

I’ve said multiple times and people here think I am hating on him. Camarda is not on the level of Tresoldi or players like Lamin Yamal. The senior level is nothing like the youth level. He needs to gradually wait until he’s about 21-22 before thinking of the senior level.

Is first touch is unplayable, his movement is generally slow and reactive and he’s still very easily forced off the ball. It’s a shame because futuro seems like the appropriate level for him but he’s advisors are blocking that path.

Few players emerging from the youth academy are immediately capable of competing at the senior level; however, a young player can progress significantly in a very short time—potentially surpassing a senior player within just a year. The difference lies in whether a club has a strategy and the patience to nurture its own homegrown talent, as opposed to clubs that lack this approach. Take the example of Palestra: he couldn’t break into the Atalanta squad, yet just a year later, he moved to Chelsea. Do you think he would have developed as much at Atalanta as he did at Cagliari? Muharemović—after two seasons at Sassuolo, he is now at Leeds and valued at 100 million. Would he have reached that level had he stayed at Juventus, watching matches from the stands? There are many such examples. Clubs often try to solve their problems immediately through transfers—sometimes hitting the mark, but frequently missing—spending a fortune on a player, while right under their noses, a homegrown talent goes to waste simply because he hasn’t quite reached that level yet.

#1513. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#1512. GdS: ‘Ambitious, surprising, Italian’ – Milan set guidelines for 2027 transfer business

When building a squad it is important to have a vision of the end goal, and AC Milan have exactly that heading into 2027.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by stating that there are no transition years when it comes to Milan. Frequently they have chosen to overhaul the squad in the summer window, and sometimes even in the winter.

For example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

The Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

The difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

Then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

It’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

Belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

#1511. Push it to the Max! Dowman, 16, becomes England U21s youngest-ever goalscorer - as Arsenal starlet scores 89th-minute winner against France

Published: 18:36 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:37 EST, 16 November 2026

Max Dowman broke another record as the 16-year-old became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England's Under-21 side on Monday night.

The Arsenal teenager has already broken a plethora of records at club level, and is now taking that to the international stage too, breaking a record set by senior team star Jude Bellingham, who scored aged 17 years and 67 days in 2020.

Dowman was called into the U21 squad for the first time this international break, and made his debut off the bench in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal on Friday.

On Monday, meanwhile, he was given a start by manager Lee Carsley, and rewarded his manager's faith with an 89th-minute winner to break the record and earn his side a 3-2 win.

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

Manager Lee Carsley said after the game: 'He played really well - he was one of four or five outstanding performances. Mikey Moore, Max, Ethan (Nwaneri), they were very good.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday

'We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball. You have to keep reminding yourself about his age. There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well.

'It's important we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'

Despite bursting onto the scene last season, Dowman has just 19 minutes to his name in the top flight this campaign as Arsenal look to defend their title.

He has played a number of games for the Gunners' U21 side, while he was sent off against League Two side Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup.

Arteta scolded his player at the time, but said: 'I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. Whether that's positive or negative. You need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed before we went out.

'If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you'd say "you don't like that reaction", but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

The Arsenal teenager, 16, broke the record held by Jude Bellingham with his late winner

'But you want to see the best and most beautiful reaction. You want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with 10 men.

'What do you expect? That's the level and that's the reaction. Whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, I'm f****d off, big time.

'This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?'

#1506. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1505. CAN 2025: The Senegal-Morocco final replayed?

Could the CAN 2025 final between Senegal and Morocco experience a new episode on the pitch? While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) must deliver its verdict to the “end of November”the hypothesis of a match to be replayed raises questions.

On January 18, 2026, Senegal won the final against Morocco (1-0), after extra time. But on March 17, the appeal jury of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) finally declared the Teranga Lions forfeited, approving a Moroccan victory with a score of 3-0. A decision contested by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), which appealed to the CAS to recover the title.

Can the CAS then decide to replay the match? The body has extensive powers of examination. It can confirm the decision of the CAF, cancel it and render a new decision, or refer the file to the competent authorities of the African Confederation. It is in particular this last possibility which could, indirectly, open the door to a new meeting. The CAS cannot, however, automatically order that a match be replayed simply because it overturns the contested decision.

A precedent exists. In 2019, after the final return of the African Champions League between Esperance de Tunis and Wydad Casablanca, CAF ordered the match to be replayed. The CAS annulled this decision, considering that the CAF executive committee was not competent, before referring the case to the African football authorities. They then declared Wydad forfeited, a decision finally confirmed by the CAS in September 2020. The match was therefore never replayed.

But the two situations are not identical. The major difference with lies in the facts. Indeed, Wydad refused to resume play after the interruption, while the Senegalese players returned to the pitch and finished the match, winning 1-0. This element could weigh in the TAS analysis.

The possibility that the final of this CAN 2025 will be replayed therefore remains legally possible, but very far from being certain. Especially since the two federations have not publicly requested a new match. After the hearing organized in October, all eyes are now turned towards the end of November, the period at which the CAS must render its decision.

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

His first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

#1501. Fondazione Milan to be celebrated at Frosinone game – the details and Gabbia’s words

Fondazione Milan will be the Match Charity Partner for AC Milan vs. Frosinone on Sunday, and Matteo Gabbia has spoken as part of the initiative.

Since 2003, the Foundation has used sport as a tool for change, reaching more than 200,000 young people through 288 projects in Italy and 25 other countries. More than €13m has been invested over the years on various projects to help those that are less fortunate.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Before kick-off on Sunday, the beneficiaries of the various schemes will take a photo with the starting lineup. They will also take part in pitch-side activities alongside Massimo Ambrosini, Daniele Massaro and Matteo Gabbia, who recently visited the Calcio Seduto project. Gabbia spoke at the event.

“It’s not easy to sum up in just a few minutes what Franco (Baresi) was like as a person and as a player. He was a key figure for the entire AC Milan club, for us kids who are trying to live up to him, and above all for all those people who always told me about his games.

“It’s always exciting for me to hear people talk about Franco and what he achieved with these colours, as a player and as a man.

“I think Franco is a legend. Fondazione Milan embodies all the beauty and importance that Baresi had. I was moved when I met and got to know the kids from the sitting football team last week.

“I’m sure that if Franco had been there, he would have been proud of everything he organized and created for this foundation.”

A post shared by Fondazione Milan (@fondazionemilan)

“I’m feeling better. It was a strange start to the season, and I was a bit disappointed personally. Hopefully, from the moment I return, it can be a positive season for me too.”

The pregame will also honour the memory of Franco Baresi and his bond with Fondazione Milan. He was a dedicated supporter of its projects, including as a member of its Board of Directors. Club employees will take part in the tribute, along with his longtime teammate and friend Daniele Massaro.

At Sunday’s match, fans can continue to support the Foundation’s projects through donations and auctions of players’ shirts, helping create new opportunities for other young people.

#1500. Nico Paz really embarrasses Real Madrid

It’s one of the sensations of the moment, in Italy, but also in Europe and around the world. To the point where in his country, in Argentina, he is considered capable of picking up the torch from Lionel Messi and becoming the new leader of the Albiceleste. It must be said that Nico Paz displays a stratospheric level with FC Como. A clearly extraordinary talent, and above all, an elegance with the ball that very few players can boast of displaying. The native of Tenerife (Spain) is the present and future of football.

And even if many have forgotten it, Nico Paz is a pure product… of Real Madrid. Trained with the Merengues, he chose to leave in the summer of 2025. During the 2026 summer transfer window, in an operation aimed at replenishing the coffers, Real Madrid exercised its buyout option of 9 million euros, before reselling him for 60 million euros to the Italian team. Next summer, the Merengues will still be able to bring him back for an amount of 80 million euros. And clearly, everything indicates that in Madrid, no one really knows what to do…

In a normal context, Real Madrid, like any other club on the planet, would have no hesitation and would already be preparing to bring him back to keep him in their squad. However, the Madrilenians have a small problem: the positions and roles where Paz could play at the Bernabéu are already well occupied, by Jude Bellingham and by Arda Güler. For many supporters and journalists, the Argentinian, as good as he is, doesn’t really have his place. And Real Madrid would therefore not necessarily need it. “Güler’s extension is to show the player that he is important, but also to tell Nico Paz that this position at Real Madrid already has an owner”for example explained Raul Varela on Radio Marca.

Clearly, what stands out is that Real Madrid don’t know what to do. The evidence, the information that comes out is contradictory. Mundo Deportivo And Libertad Digital indicate this Thursday that the club is counting on him for the coming season, while others explained that Mourinho is not necessarily seduced and that Paz is not a priority. Then, you also have to know the intentions of the player, coveted by other big teams. Several media explain, logically, that he does not want to play supporting roles, and that he would only return to Real Madrid to have an important role. Similar situation for his teammate and also ex-Madrilenian Jacobo Ramon. In any case, his agent’s phone is likely to ring a lot in the coming months since Manchester United are already on the case…

#1499. Man United's first woman on their backroom team, the fitness enforcer, a scorpion-kicking goalkeeper coach... and his son! Meet Mauricio Pochettino's team of experts flying in to whip United's flops into shape

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

When the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff

That was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

In 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

They now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

He loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

After meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where plans for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

For example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his new-found fame.

When they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

To give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019)

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

While with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

When Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

The goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

Jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

They say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

Hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding new areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding new areas to his game

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG)

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH

The son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was said that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is important to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he said. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'

#1498. Çelik pulled from Türkiye XI with left hamstring tightness as Kalulu is already out

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

The league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

#1497. MN: Eyes on Manchester – the City and United duo Milan want to bring back to Italy

AC Milan are looking for opportunities to bolster the squad ahead of next season, with a particular eye on the north of England.

According to MilanNews, Milan are eyeing Manchester for the January transfer window, but also for next summer. The directors are currently in a phase of monitoring certain situations that could develop later, to their benefit.

The Rossoneri are also interested in players whose contracts are expiring within the next 18 months, as was the case with Mario Gila this summer, who signed for the Diavolo one year before his contract with Lazio expires.

Bruno Fernandes is one to watch for the upcoming summer transfer window, with his contract expiring in June 2027 but with an option to extend. United’s attempts to extend his deal have so far been unsuccessful, likely due to the player’s desire to try something else.

Fernandes has played at an incredible level in the Premier League in recent years, winning Player of the Year for 2025-26. So far, he has made 341 official appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists.

He’s a key player for the Portuguese national team and he would provide leadership that the squad could lose if players like Luka Modric leave. Moreover, his past in Italy – where he had spells at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria – could help him integrate more quickly and effectively.

Fernandes also shares the same agency as Ruben Amorim. The relationship between the two is excellent, and already this summer the Rossoneri had inquired about a possible move for the former Sporting star.

At the other Manchester club, however, there’s an old acquaintance of Italian football who could come back into fashion as early as January: Mateo Kovacic. His contract also expires at the end of the campaign, and he could come in to add depth too.

Given the increasingly certain departure of youngster Christian Comotto, an experienced player like Kovacic – at the right price, in terms of wages – could be useful for Amorim. His situation is being watched, but there will be competition from other clubs, likely in Italy too.

#1496. McKennie says USA players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United

Weston McKennie has said USA players could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, days after his national team coach took the job there. Juventus, already without Thuram and Locatelli, now face pressure to rule out a mid-season sale.

The question put to Weston McKennie was whether USA players might follow their coach to Old Trafford. His answer was that it could potentially happen.

McKennie called the speculation inevitable. He said many USA players are due to change clubs within the next year, calciomercato.com reported.

Pochettino was asked about the same subject. He said now was not the right time to discuss it. He added that United are among the very top clubs and a dream for many players.

Pochettino and his staff remain in charge of the USA for two games against Haiti, on 14 and 17 November. United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

The comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s plans and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

#1493. GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s plans.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

#1492. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

#1491. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.
